claims.statement: The DP-3 editions form a supersession chain: 2012-11 is superseded by 2020-08 for policies effective on or after 2020-08-01, and 2020-08 is superseded by 2026-01 for policies effective on or after 2026-01-01; each superseded edition remains applicable to policies written under it.

DP-3 uses broad direct-physical-loss wording for Coverage A and Coverage B subject to exclusions, while personal property under Coverage C is limited to the applicable covered-peril schedule; the 2012-11 form states this as open-peril building coverage versus expressly described perils for Coverage C.

Coverage A settlement differs by edition: 2012-11 requires at least 80% of pre-loss replacement cost for replacement-cost settlement, 2020-08 requires 90% of replacement cost, and the supplied 2026-01 Coverage A wording states that the most payable is 80% while separately placing roof surfacing on an actual-cash-value basis; the 2026 text should not be supplemented with earlier editions' threshold rules.
Coverage B is limited to 10% of Coverage A in 2012-11 and 2020-08, and increases to 15% of Coverage A in 2026-01; the 2026 form also limits payment to the insured's interest or legal responsibility.

Coverage C has a stated limit of 0% of Coverage A in all three supplied DP-3 editions, while later editions expressly broaden or detail locations and handling such as temporarily away, newly acquired residence, storage, moving or transport, and other specified locations subject to the applicable form.

Coverage D is limited to 20% of Coverage A in 2012-11, 25% in 2020-08, and 30% in 2026-01; the 2020 form includes a civil-authority Additional Living Expense provision, while the 2026 form limits fair-rental-value payment to actual lost rent while the rented part is unfit and may limit it to the reasonable restoration period when repair or replacement is not prompt.

Across the editions, DP-3 excludes flood and surface water, below-ground water, sewer or drain backup absent applicable coverage, earth movement, ordinance-or-law costs unless provided, gradual seepage or leakage, faulty work, deterioration, and other listed causes, while allowing resulting or ensuing direct physical loss only where the applicable edition says the resulting loss is separately covered.

The 2026-01 peril schedule enumerates covered causes including fire or lightning, windstorm or hail, explosion, riot or civil commotion, aircraft, vehicles, smoke, vandalism or malicious mischief, falling objects, weight of ice snow or sleet, accidental system discharge, freezing, and artificially generated electrical current; Coverage C remains subject to a covered peril and its stated exclusions.

Coverage E monetary limits change by edition: 2012-11 provides 5% additional debris removal, a 5% Coverage A vegetation aggregate with a $500 per-item cap, and a $500 fire-department service charge; 2020-08 uses 10%, a 10% vegetation aggregate with a $750 per-item cap, and $750; 2026-01 uses 15%, a 10% vegetation aggregate with a $1,000 per-item cap, and $1,000, while also detailing additional mitigation, removal, drying, emergency-repair, and ordinance-or-law provisions.

The editions impose different claim-settlement mechanics: the minimum Section I deductible is $500 in 2012-11, $1,000 in 2020-08, and $1,500 in 2026-01; proof of loss is due within 60 days after request in 2012-11 and 2026-01 and 90 days after request in 2020-08; payment follows the stated 60-day, 45-day, and 30-day rules respectively; appraisal determines amount of loss rather than coverage.

DP 04 95 Water Backup is an optional DP endorsement that controls conflicting base-form language when attached, covers direct physical loss from sewer or drain backup and sump overflow, retains exclusions for flood and other causes, has a $5,000 aggregate limit, and applies a $1,000 deductible to the covered water-backup loss.

The Florida DP 01 09 overlay controls conflicts, imposes a 2% to 10% windstorm-and-hail deductible, requires 45 days' notice for an increase, defines a Named Storm Period through 72 hours after designation ends, and supplies Florida cancellation and claim-handling deadlines including 14-day acknowledgment, 90-business-day decision after requested items, and 20-business-day payment after acceptance.

The Texas DP 01 45 overlay applies to Texas property and Texas-law losses, controls conflicts, imposes a 1% to 5% windstorm-or-hail deductible, requires 30 days' notice for a deductible increase, defines a 72-hour post-designation Named Storm Period, and supplies Texas cancellation and claim-handling deadlines including 15-day acknowledgment, 15-business-day decision after requested items, and five-business-day payment after acceptance.

All DP-3 editions require notice, mitigation, preservation and inspection of damaged property, records or inventories, cooperation, proof of loss, and preservation of recovery rights; the 2020 and 2026 editions contain prejudice or materiality limits in specified duty provisions, so those later formulations must not be back-applied to the 2012 edition.

The 2020-08 and 2026-01 filing memoranda are interpretation aids rather than policy terms: the 2020 memorandum describes clarification of terminology, coverage, limits, deductibles, duties, and exclusions, while the 2026 memorandum says it retains the overall dwelling-policy structure while clarifying terminology, organization, conditions, exclusions, and coverage provisions.
